title: 3-Read Friday #55: Thinking Hard, Relationships, and Don Steward's Archive
author: Craig Barton
summary: In issue 55, Barton curates a research-heavy trio alongside a personal tribute. He first recommends Andrew Watson's summary of a meta-analysis on the relationship between perceived mental effort and perceived learning, describing Watson's recurring gift for extracting classroom implications from research. He then points to Jo Castelino's post on building relationships with students, framing it around the question of what actually motivates students to love learning. His third pick honours the late maths task designer Don Steward via Tom Francome's tribute post about digitising Steward's paper archive, which Barton -- a fellow maths teacher -- frames with obvious personal enthusiasm ('I can't wait to get stuck in'). A reader comment flags that the link to Castelino's post was broken at the time of sending, which the archive resolves by locating the article directly on her blog.
points: Barton values Watson's writing specifically for its consistent 'translate research into classroom implications' function, not just for reporting findings.

His framing of the Castelino pick as a question ('what motivates students to love learning?') rather than a summary shows he's using the newsletter to pose open questions to readers, not just hand down conclusions.

The obvious personal enthusiasm in the Don Steward tribute ('one for the maths geeks... I can't wait to get stuck in') marks a rare moment where Barton's own subject-specialist identity as a maths teacher visibly drives the pick.
The broken-link comment thread on this issue is a reminder that even a heavily-read curation newsletter has real production friction -- Barton's picks depend on fragile third-party blog URLs.
quotes: Andrew always does a great job of picking out an interesting piece of research and extracting the key implications for the classroom.
This latest instalment delves into a paper investigating the relationship between the amount of mental effort students put into a task and their perception of how much they are learning.
What motivates students to love learning? Is it the personality of the teacher or something else? Jo digs into this fascinating area.
Don Steward, who sadly passed away in 2020, was one of the greatest task designers of all time.
Tom and the team at Loughborough University have completed the monumental task of digitising Don’s paper-based archive.
